name: Banded Ankle Eversion
description: Sit with the legs out in front, a band anchored to one side and looped around the ball of the foot. Keeping the shin still, turn the sole of the foot outward against the band, then return slowly. This trains the peroneals — the muscles running down the outside of the lower leg that stop the ankle rolling inward. They are the group that fails in a classic lateral ankle sprain and the group that stays weak for years afterward, so this is the highest-value strengthening move for a previously sprained ankle. Pair it with banded inversion (band anchored on the opposite side, turning the sole inward) to train the tibialis posterior on the other side of the joint.
